title: Ultrasonic Echo Timing Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: See the HC-SR04 trigger pulse, the sound's round trip, and the Echo pin on one timeline, and convert the echo time in microseconds to centimeters with duration / 58.

educational.topic: Ultrasonic distance sensing with the HC-SR04
learningObjectives: Convert an echo pulse duration in microseconds into a distance in centimeters with duration_us / 58.
Explain that 58 comes from the round trip (2x) divided by the speed of sound, 0.0343 cm per microsecond.
Explain why a missing echo requires a timeout in read_ultrasonic_cm().
prerequisites: Converting meters to centimeters and seconds to microseconds

controls.label: Fire sensor
controls.purpose: Replay one measurement in slow motion.

controls.label: Soft surface (weak echo)
controls.purpose: Weaken the echo; past 250 cm it is lost.

controls.label: Distance
controls.purpose: Distance to the wall. The wall can also be dragged.

assumptions: Echo rises after the 200 microsecond, 8-cycle burst and stays HIGH for the round-trip time.
Valid echoes return from 2 to 400 cm, or up to 250 cm from a soft surface.
limitations: Some modules drop Echo LOW after about 38 ms with no echo; the sim keeps it HIGH.
Wall angle and size are not modeled.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Linked representations: scene, pin timeline, and filled-in formula
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Static timeline and math for the current distance, with an optional slow-motion replay
keyQuestions: Why does the formula divide by 58 instead of by the speed of sound?
What does the Echo pin do while the sound is flying?
What happens to read_ultrasonic_cm() if the echo never comes back?
commonMisconceptions: The echo time is for a one-way trip.
The Echo pin pulses only when the sound returns.
The speed of sound is the same at every temperature.
assessmentOpportunities: Convert a 2900 microsecond echo into centimeters.
Derive 58 from 343 m/s and the round trip.
Explain the 0 C error and propose a timeout for missing echoes.
